title: Lattices after a finite stratification
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\cO_E$ and a uniformizer $\pi_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. The standing schemes are separated schemes of finite type over the fixed field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, $p\ne\ell$. The coefficients $E_X$ and $\cO_{E,X}$ are the pullbacks of the condensed topological rings $E$ and $\cO_E$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Modules mean module objects in abelian sheaves on the small pro-étale site [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Here lisse means locally free of finite rank for the pro-étale topology, with ranks allowed to vary; a lattice is a lisse $\cO_{E,X}$-submodule whose localization at $\ell$ is the given $E_X$-module. A finite stratification means a finite disjoint covering by locally closed subschemes [def-constructible-stratification].

Statements with coefficients $\cO_E/\pi_E^n$ reach $E$-coefficients only through integral
lattices. A lisse $E_X$-module need not have a lattice on all of $X$, but it has one on each
stratum of a finite stratification, and for dévissage arguments this suffices. A global
lattice can fail to exist when $X$ is not normal. Let $X$ be a projective line with $0$ and
$\infty$ glued to a node, and let $Y\to X$ be the infinite chain of projective lines covering
it, an étale $\mathbf Z$-torsor. Descending $E_Y$ along $Y\to X$, with the generator of
$\mathbf Z$ acting by multiplication by $\ell$, gives a lisse $E_X$-module $L$ of rank one.
Since $Y$ is connected, a lattice in $L|_Y\cong E_Y$ is a constant lattice $\pi_E^m\cO_E$, and
no such lattice is stable under multiplication by $\ell$; so $L$ has no lattice on $X$. On the
open stratum $X\smallsetminus\{\text{node}\}\cong\mathbf G_m$ the torsor is trivial and $L$ is
constant.

Let $X$ be a standing scheme and $L$ a lisse $E_X$-module. There is a finite stratification
of $X$ by locally closed subschemes $S$ such that each $L|_S$ contains a lisse
$\cO_{E,S}$-submodule $L_0$ with $L_0[1/\ell]=L|_S$.

proof.text: A field is Noetherian. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X$ Noetherian. A finite affine cover has Noetherian underlying charts by [lem-sc-affine-noetherian-underlying-space]; an ascending chain of opens stabilizes on each chart, hence on $X$ at the maximum of the finitely many indices. By [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-compact-subsets] every open and every affine intersection is quasi-compact, so $X$ is qcqs.

source.place: Standing finite-type hypothesis before Sheaf of lattices

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficient-realizations] to identify pulled condensed coefficients with continuous ones, compatibly with $A=\cO_E\to E$. Its total-disconnectedness hypothesis holds: disjoint clopen ultrametric balls separate points of $E$, and $A$ inherits this. Module-object actions are precisely the sectionwise module laws, so these ring isomorphisms transport the modules and their inclusions. By [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-invert-ell], scalar extension is inversion of $\ell$. The same identifications apply on all schemes below.

By [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-etale-local-lattice], choose a qcqs étale surjection $p:V\to X$ and locally finite free $M$ with $E_V\otimes M\cong p^*L$. Its unit inclusion is injective on free charts because $A\to E$ is injective, so it embeds as a lattice in $p^*L$.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-stratified-finite] to $p$. On each stratum $S$, its base change $p_S$ is finite étale; it is surjective, since for a point of $S$ a point of the nonempty fibre of $p$ survives the residue-field extension defining the fibre of $p_S$. Part (2) of [det-lem-coefficient-heart-common-stratification] gives that $L|_S$ is lisse. Apply [lem-sfb-lattice-pullback] along $V\times_X S\to V$ to obtain an embedded lattice $M_S\subseteq p_S^*(L|_S)$.

By [lem-sfb-finite-etale-trace-image], define $L_0$ as the integral trace image. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-etale-local-split], étale splitting neighbourhoods cover $S$; there the image is the sum of the sheet lattices. The sheet set is nonempty on every nonempty neighbourhood because $p_S$ is surjective.

Trivialize $L|_S$ pro-étale locally. By [lem-weil-pbc-lattice-sheaf-locally-constant] every sheet lattice is a section of the constant sheaf on $\operatorname{GL}_r(E)/\operatorname{GL}_r(A)$, hence locally one coset $g_j$: a fixed lattice $\Lambda_j=g_jA^r\subseteq E^r$. Refine the finitely many covers successively to fix them together. By [lem-sfb-finite-sum-lattice], $\Lambda=\sum_j\Lambda_j$ has a basis homeomorphism $A^r\simeq\Lambda$. By [lem-sfb-continuous-lattice-sum], the sheet-sheaf sum is the continuous-function sheaf of $\Lambda$, free over $A$, with inclusion inducing an isomorphism after rationalization.

These are local assertions: local freeness is the definition of lisse; the local inverses to rationalization agree and glue. Hence $L_0$ is a lattice on each stratum. Discard empty strata; empty $X$ has the empty stratification, and rank zero gives the zero lattice.
